doc.title: Wilson "Chembo" Corniel interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, November 15, 2019

title: Learning theory first and respecting each genre's laws
summary: Rowe suggests further interviews; Corniel says musicians must learn theory and listening before playing and respect every genre.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Advice to young musicians starting out

blocks.x: Right. Well I envision a part 2, 3 and 4 of an interview with you.
Yeah that’s what I’m thinking. And you speak very eloquently about the music.

Sure, sure. You have to, you’ve got to understand it that way you know. People just can’t grab a horn and okay let’s play. Let’s play what? You know? But once you start playing and now, you know, but you’ve got to learn all these things first. You’ve got to have that theory first before playing. You know you have, like classes where you learn and you play your horn, your instrument, but what are you playing? Then you’ve got the theory part of it, the other part, which you’ve got to sit down and listen. I could put records on for you, what’s he doing here, what kind of style is this here, and you’ve got to have that other balance so you could know first of all what are you doing, and then you grab your horn. That’s another life right there you know? So it goes with every instrument you play, in any genre, classical, rock, anything you do. They have their own laws too. You know? I go play rock & roll, I paint my hair pink, you know? I color it pink, I do what you want to do, put sunglasses on, pierce my ear, my nose, hey, jump up and down but I’ll play my stuff.
